translations.text: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

The Lord handed it over to him, along with Jehoiakim king of Judah and the vessels of the Lord’s house. He brought some of the vessels of the Lord’s house to the land of Shinar, to the temple of his idol, and put the vessels in his idol’s treasury.
The king told Ashpenaz, the chief of the eunuchs, to bring some of the Israelites, including some of royal descent and some of the nobles:

young men without any defect, handsome in appearance, skilled in wisdom, knowledgeable and discerning, and physically capable of serving in the king’s palace. He was to teach them the literature and language of the Chaldeans.
The king assigned them a daily allowance from the king’s food and from the wine he drank. They were to be brought up for three years and then enter the king’s service.
Among them were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, from the people of Judah.
The chief of the eunuchs gave them names: he called Daniel Belteshazzar, Hananiah Shadrach, Mishael Meshach, and Azariah Abednego.
Daniel resolved not to eat the king’s food or drink the wine he drank, and he asked the chief of the eunuchs not to make him eat it.
God granted Daniel favor and compassion in the eyes of the chief of the eunuchs.

The chief of the eunuchs said to Daniel, “I am afraid of my lord the king, who has prescribed your food and drink. He might see that your faces look worse than those of the young men your own age, and the king would cut off my head.”
Daniel said to the steward whom the chief of the eunuchs had put in charge of Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah:
Test your servants for ten days, and let us be given vegetables to eat and water to drink.
“Then compare our appearance with the appearance of the young men who eat the king’s food, and deal with your servants according to what you see.”
He agreed to their request and tested them for ten days.
After ten days, he saw that their faces looked better and their bodies were better nourished than those of all the young men who ate the king’s food.
The steward used to take their allotted food and the wine they were to drink for himself, and give them seeds to eat and water to drink.
God gave these four young men knowledge and understanding in all literature and wisdom, and Daniel understood all visions and dreams.
When the period the king had prescribed was over, the chief of the eunuchs brought them before King Nebuchadnezzar.
The king spoke with them, and among them all he found no one like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they entered the king’s service.
In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his kingdom.
Daniel remained until the first year of King Cyrus.
In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, Nebuchadnezzar had a dream. His spirit was troubled, and sleep came over him.
The king ordered the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans to be summoned to tell the king his dream. They came and stood before the king.
The king said to them, “I have had a dream, and my spirit is troubled because I want to understand the dream.”
The Chaldeans spoke before the king in Aramaic, saying, “O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will explain its meaning.”
The king answered the Chaldeans, “What I have said is firm: unless you tell me the dream and its meaning, you will be cut limb from limb, and your houses will be plundered.
But if you tell me the dream and its meaning, you will receive gifts, wealth, and great honor from me. Only tell me the dream and its meaning!”
They answered him again, saying, “Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will explain its meaning.”
The king answered, “I know for certain that you are asking for time because you have seen that my word is firm.

If you do not tell me the dream, there is only one sentence for you. You have agreed to speak lies and empty words before me until the time passes. But tell me the dream, so that I may know that you can also explain its meaning to me.”
The Chaldeans answered the king, “There is no one on earth who can reveal what the king asks. Nor has any great and powerful king ever asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean.
What the king asks is difficult, and there is no one who can reveal it before the king except the gods, who do not dwell among human beings.”
Then the king became extremely angry, and in great rage he ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be destroyed.
The decree went out, and the wise men were being killed. They also sought Daniel and his companions to kill them.
Then Daniel considered the matter, took counsel, and spoke to Arioch, the king’s chief executioner, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
“Why has such a harsh decree gone out from the king?” Then Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.
Daniel asked the king to give him time, so that he could make the interpretation known to the king.
Then Daniel went to his house and told his companions Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah about this matter,
so that they would ask the God of heaven for mercy concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his companions would not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision at night, and Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
Daniel responded and said, “May the name of the Lord be blessed forever and ever, for wisdom and might belong to him.
He changes times and seasons; he removes kings and establishes kings. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who have understanding.
He reveals deep and hidden things. He knows what is in the darkness, and light is with him.
To you, God of my ancestors, I give thanks and praise, for you have given me wisdom and might. Now you have made known to me what we asked of you, and you have made the king’s matter known to me.”

At that very moment Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had ordered to kill the wise men of Babylon. He went and said to him, “Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon. Instead, bring me before the king, and I will show the king the interpretation.”
Then Arioch hurriedly brought Daniel before the king and said to him, “I have found a man among the captives from Judah who will make the interpretation known to the king.”
The king responded and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Can you show me the dream I saw and its interpretation?”
Daniel answered before the king, “Neither wise men, magi, sorcerers, nor enchanters can show the king the mystery that the king asks about.

But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, who will make known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the latter days. This is your dream and the vision in your mind while you were on your bed.
As for you, O king, thoughts arose in your mind about what would happen in the future, and the revealer of mysteries made known to you what would happen.

As for me, this mystery was revealed to me not because I have more wisdom than all the living, but so that the interpretation might be made known to the king and you might know what you were thinking in your heart.
You, O king, were looking, and there was a great statue whose brilliance was extraordinary. It stood before you, and its appearance was terrifying.
Its head was of fine gold, its chest and arms of silver, and its belly and thighs of bronze.
Its legs were iron, and its feet were partly iron and partly clay.
You saw a stone cut out without hands. It struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and crushed them completely.

Then the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold were crushed together and became like chaff from a summer threshing floor. A strong wind carried them away, and no place was found for them. The stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
This is the dream, and he told its interpretation before the king.
You, O king, are king of kings. The Most High God has given you a mighty kingdom and honor.
Wherever human beings live, he has given them, the birds of the sky, and the wild animals into your hands and made you ruler over them all. You are the head of gold.
After you another kingdom will arise, inferior to yours, and another, a third kingdom of bronze, will rule over the whole earth.
A fourth kingdom will be strong as iron. Just as iron crushes and pulverizes everything, so it too will crush and subdue everything.

As for the feet and toes you saw, partly of potter’s clay and partly of iron, the kingdom will be divided. Yet some of the solidity of iron will be in it, just as you saw iron mixed with earthen clay.
As for the toes of the feet you saw, partly of iron and partly of clay, part of the kingdom will be strong and part will be broken.
As you saw iron mixed with earthen clay, so they will intermingle through human offspring, but they will not hold together, just as iron does not mix with clay.

In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will establish a kingdom that will never be destroyed. It will not leave its rule to another people, but will crush and put an end to all these kingdoms, and it will stand forever.

Just as you saw a stone cut out of the mountain without hands, which crushed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold, the great God has made known to you what will happen in the latter days. The dream is certain, and its interpretation is trustworthy.”
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell facedown and bowed before Daniel, and ordered incense and offerings to be presented to him.
The king said to Daniel, “Truly, your God is the God of gods, the Lord of kings, and the revealer of mysteries, since you were able to reveal this mystery.”
Then the king promoted Daniel, gave him many gifts, and made him ruler over the whole land of Babylon. He appointed him chief over all the military commanders and all the wise men of Babylon.
Daniel made a request to the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the administration of the province of Babylon. Daniel himself remained at the king’s court.
King Nebuchadnezzar made a gold statue sixty cubits high and six cubits wide. He set it up on the plain of Dura in the land of Babylon.

King Nebuchadnezzar sent word to assemble the military commanders, lords, governors, chief officials, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the provincial authorities, to come to the dedication of the new statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

Then all the military commanders, lords, governors, chief officials, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the provincial authorities assembled and came to the dedication of the new statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up. They stood before the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
The herald called out loudly, saying, “You are commanded, peoples, nations, and languages:
“When you hear the sound of the horn, flute, lyre, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, you must fall down and worship the gold statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.”
Whoever does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into a furnace of blazing fire.”

Whenever the peoples heard the sound of the horn, flute, lyre, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, all the peoples, nations, and speakers of every language fell down and worshiped the gold statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
At that very time, some Chaldean men came forward and brought accusations against the Jews.
They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, “O king, live forever!
“You, O king, issued a command that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, flute, lyre, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music must fall down and worship the gold statue you have set up.
Whoever does not fall down and worship is to be thrown into the blazing furnace.

There are Jewish men here whom you appointed over the affairs of the province of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men pay no attention to you, O king. They do not serve your god or worship the gold statue you have set up.”
Then King Nebuchadnezzar, in rage and fury, ordered Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to be brought in. They were brought before the king.
King Nebuchadnezzar said to them, “Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you do not serve my god or worship the gold statue I have set up?

Now, if you are ready, when you hear the sound of the horn, flute, lyre, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, fall down and worship the statue I have made. But if you do not worship, you will immediately be thrown into a furnace of blazing fire. And who is your god, that he should rescue you from my hands?”
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered King Nebuchadnezzar, “We have no need to give you an answer about this matter.
For our God, whom we serve, has the power to rescue us from the furnace of blazing fire, and he will deliver us from your hands, O king.
But know, O king, that we will not serve your god or worship the gold statue you have set up.”
Then King Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and his expression changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He ordered the furnace to be heated seven times hotter than it was usually heated.
He ordered men of great strength to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and throw them into the furnace of blazing fire.
Then those men bound them in their trousers, footwear, clothes, and hats, and threw them into the furnace of blazing fire.
Because the king’s command was urgent and the furnace was heated to an extreme temperature, the flame of the blazing fire killed those men who had accused Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
Those three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell bound into the middle of the furnace of blazing fire.

Then King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished and stood up in great fear. He said to his officials, “Did we not throw three men, bound, into the furnace of blazing fire?” They answered the king, “Yes, certainly, O king.”
The king said, “Look! I see men unbound, walking around in the fire, and they are unharmed. The appearance of the fourth resembles a son of the gods.”

Then King Nebuchadnezzar approached the entrance of the furnace of blazing fire and said, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out! Come here!” Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out of the fiery furnace.

All the peoples, military commanders, rulers, lords, and the king’s nobles gathered together. They saw that the fire had had no power over these men’s bodies: the hair on their heads was not singed, their trousers were not burned, and no smell of fire clung to them.

King Nebuchadnezzar spoke and said, “Blessed is the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his angel and rescued his servants who trusted in him. They rejected the king’s command and gave up their bodies rather than serve or worship any god except their own God.”

“And so I command that anyone of any people, nation, or language who blasphemes against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego shall be cut limb from limb, and their houses shall be plundered, because there is no other god who can rescue in this way.”
Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the region of Babylon.
King Nebuchadnezzar wrote to all peoples, nations, and speakers of every language who live throughout the earth: “May peace abound for you.”
I thought it good to make known the signs and wonders that the Most High God has performed.
How great are his signs, and how mighty his wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his dominion lasts from generation to generation.
Do not give us up completely, for your name’s sake, and do not annul your covenant.
Do not withdraw your mercy and kindness from us, for the sake of Abraham your friend, for the sake of Isaac your servant, and for the sake of Israel your holy one.
You promised them that you would multiply their descendants like the stars in heaven and like the sand on the seashore.
For now, Lord, we have been brought lower than all the peoples, and today we are scattered throughout the earth because of our offenses and our sins.
At this time there is no chief or ruler, no prophet or leader, no altar, sacrifices, or offerings, and no place where we can offer incense or a sacrifice and find favor and mercy.
But with a broken heart and a humble spirit, here we have been offered up to be burned in the fire.
We ask that the offering of ourselves today may be worth more than bulls, rams, and many fat lambs. Do not let your servants be put to shame, for those who trust in you are not put to shame.
Even now we follow you wholeheartedly. We have feared you, and we seek your face.
Lord, do not put us to shame, but deal with us according to your abundant kindness and your great mercy.
Deliver us according to your many wonders, and bring glory to your name, Lord, for the sake of your great name.
Let all those who speak evil against your servants be put to shame. Let them be put to shame despite all their might, and let their strength desert them.
May they know that you alone are the one God, and that you are praised in all your works.
Those who were heating the fiery furnace did not stop. They kept throwing naphtha, pitch, sulfur, reeds, and vine branches into it.
The flame of the fire roared and rose forty-nine cubits above the furnace.
The fire burned and destroyed everyone it found around the furnace, both Chaldeans and accusers.
But the angel of dew went down with Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael into the fiery furnace and drove the fiery flame out of the furnace.
He made the middle of the furnace like a dew-laden breeze. The fire did not come near them, not even a little; it neither harmed nor distressed them.
Then all three, with one voice, praised and blessed God from within the fiery furnace, saying:
Blessed are you, Lord, God of our ancestors. You are praised and exalted forever. Blessed is the holy name of your glory. You are praised and exalted forever.
Blessed are you in your holy temple. You are praised and exalted forever.
Blessed are you who see the depths and sit enthroned upon the cherubim. You are praised and exalted forever.
Blessed are you on your royal throne. You are praised and exalted forever.
Blessed are you in the expanse of heaven. You are praised and exalted forever.
All you works of the Lord, bless the Lord. Praise and exalt him forever.
All you angels of the Lord, bless the Lord. Praise and exalt him forever.
You heavens of the Lord, bless the Lord. Praise and exalt him forever.
You waters above the heavens, bless the Lord. Praise him and exalt him forever. All you who fear the Lord, bless the Lord. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all the Lord’s hosts. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, sun and moon. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, stars in heaven. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, rain and dew. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, waters and winds. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Fire and heat, bless the Lord. Praise him and exalt him forever. All you souls of the righteous, bless the Lord. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Frost and heat, bless the Lord. Praise him and exalt him forever. Summer and winter, bless the Lord. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, snow and ice. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, nights and days. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, light and darkness. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, lightning and clouds. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, earth. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, mountains and hills. Praise him and exalt him forever.
All you hills of the earth, bless the Lord. Praise him and exalt him forever. Everything that grows on the earth, bless the Lord. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, fountains and all springs. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, seas and rivers. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, fish and everything that moves in the waters. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all birds of the sky. Praise him and exalt him forever.
All you wild animals and livestock, bless the Lord. Praise him and exalt him forever. Everything that crawls on the earth, bless the Lord. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all human beings. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all who belong to the house of Israel. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all the Lord’s priests. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all the Lord’s servants. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all the souls and spirits of the righteous. Praise him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, you who are blameless and humble in heart. Praise him and exalt him forever.

Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, bless the Lord. Praise him and exalt him forever. For he rescued us from death, saved our lives from the power of Sheol, delivered us from the burning flame, and brought us out from the midst of the fire.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, and his kindness lasts forever. Praise him and exalt him forever.
All you who fear God, bless the God of gods. Praise him and exalt him forever. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, and his kindness lasts forever.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and at rest in my palace.
I saw a dream and was disturbed, and the visions in my head troubled me.
I ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be brought before me, so that they could tell me the interpretation of the dream.
The sorcerers, enchanters, Chaldeans, and magicians came before me, and I told them the dream, but they did not make its interpretation known to me.
At last Daniel came before me, the one named Belteshazzar after the name of my god, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods. I told him the dream.

Belteshazzar, chief of the wise men, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and that no mystery is hidden from you. In the vision of my dream I see a vision in my mind; tell me its interpretation.
As I watched on my bed, there was a tree in the middle of the earth, and its height was great.
The tree grew tall and strong, and its height reached heaven. It was visible to all the ends of the earth.

Its leaves were beautiful, its fruit abundant, and it had food for all living creatures. All the wild animals lived beneath it, and all the birds of the sky nested in its branches. Every living creature was fed from it.
As I watched in the visions in my head while on my bed, there was a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven.

He called out loudly and said, “Cut down the tree and lop off its branches. Strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the animals flee from beneath it and the birds of the sky from its branches.

But leave its rooted stump in the ground, bound with iron and bronze, among the tender grass of the field. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let his dwelling be with the wild animals among the grass of the earth.
Let his mind be changed from a human mind, and let an animal's mind be given to him. Let seven periods of time pass over him.

The sentence is by the watcher's decree, and the decision by the holy one's command, so that the living may know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity. He gives it to whomever he wishes and sets the lowliest of people over it.”

This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. Now you, Belteshazzar, tell me its interpretation, because none of the wise men of my kingdom can make it known to me. But you, Daniel, can, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.

Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was stunned for about an hour, and his thoughts troubled him. The king said, “Belteshazzar, do not let the dream and its interpretation trouble you.” Daniel answered, “My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies!
The tree you saw, which grew large and strong, whose height reached to heaven and which was visible to all the ends of the earth,

whose leaves were beautiful, whose fruit was abundant, and which had food for all living creatures—all the wild animals lived beneath it, all the birds of the sky nested in its branches, and every living creature was fed from it.
It is you, O king, who have become strong and great. You have grown and reached heaven, and your dominion extends to all the ends of the earth.

And the king saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven, calling out loudly and saying, ‘Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave its rooted stump in the ground, bound with iron and bronze, among the tender grass of the field. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let his dwelling be with the wild animals among the grass of the earth. Let his mind be changed from a human mind, and let an animal's mind be given to him, until seven periods of time pass over him.’
This is the interpretation, O king: the decree of the Most High has come upon my lord the king.

You will be driven away from people, and your dwelling will be with the wild animals. You will be fed grass like an ox and drenched with the dew of heaven. Seven periods of time will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity. He gives it to whomever he wishes and sets the lowliest of people over it.
And the command to leave the tree's rooted stump means that your kingdom will remain secure for you once you know that authority comes from heaven.
Therefore, may my advice be acceptable to you: redeem your sins through charitable giving and your wrongdoing through mercy toward the weak, until your offenses are removed from you.”
All these things happened to King Nebuchadnezzar.
After twelve months, King Nebuchadnezzar was walking on the roof of his royal palace in Babylon.
He said, “Is this not great Babylon, which I built as the seat of my kingdom, for my mighty dominion and my honor?”
While the words were still in the king's mouth, a voice came from heaven: “To you, King Nebuchadnezzar, it is declared: your kingdom has passed from you.

You will be driven away from people, and your dwelling will be with the wild animals. You will be fed grass like an ox and drenched with the dew of heaven. Seven periods of time will pass over you, until you know that God Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity. He gives it to whomever he wishes and sets the lowliest of people over it.”

At that very hour the declaration was fulfilled against King Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven away from human beings, ate grass like an ox, and was drenched with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like an eagle's feathers and his nails like a bird's claws.

When those days were over, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my reason returned to me. I blessed the Most High and praised and honored the one who lives forever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion and whose kingdom endures from generation to generation.

All the inhabitants of the earth are counted as nothing before him. He does whatever he wishes among the armies of heaven and the inhabitants of the earth. No one can restrain his hand or say to him, “What are you doing?”
At that time my reason returned to me. My nobles and military commanders sought me out, and I was established over my kingdom. Still greater majesty was added to me.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, exalt, and honor the King of heaven, whose deeds are all true and whose ways are just. He is able to humble those who walk in pride.
King Belshazzar held a great banquet for a thousand of his nobles, and he drank wine in front of the thousand.

Under the influence of his wine, Belshazzar ordered the gold and silver vessels that his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem to be brought, so that the king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines could drink from them.
Then they brought the gold vessels that he had taken from the temple of God in Jerusalem, and the king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines drank from them.
They drank wine and praised the gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
At that very moment, the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote opposite the lamp on the plaster of the wall in the king’s palace. The king saw the hand as it wrote.
Then the king’s color changed, his thoughts troubled him, his hip joints gave way, and his knees knocked against each other.

The king shouted loudly for the enchanters, Chaldeans, magi, and wise men to be brought in. The king said to the wise men of Babylon, “Whoever reads this writing and tells me its interpretation will be clothed in purple, with a gold chain around his neck, and will rule as third in the kingdom.”
Then the king’s wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or make its interpretation known to the king.
Then King Belshazzar became greatly troubled, his face changed color, and his nobles were bewildered.
Because of what the king and his nobles were saying, the queen entered the banquet hall. She said to the king, “O king, live forever! Do not let your thoughts trouble you or your color change.”

“There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him. In your father’s days, enlightenment, understanding, and great wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, were found in him. King Nebuchadnezzar, your father, appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, magi, and Chaldeans.”

“For an exceptional spirit, knowledge, and understanding were found in him—in Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. He interprets dreams, unravels riddles, and unties knots. Now let Daniel be called, and he will explain the interpretation.”
Then Daniel came in before the king. The king said to Daniel, “Are you Daniel, one of the captives from Judah whom my father the king brought from Judah?”
“I have heard about you that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and that enlightenment, understanding, and exceptional wisdom have been found in you.”
“The enchanters were brought before me to read this writing and tell me its interpretation, but they could not make the interpretation of the matter known to me.”

“But I have heard about you that you can give interpretations and untie knots. If you can read this writing and make its interpretation known to me, you will be clothed in purple, with a gold chain around your neck, and you will rule as third in the kingdom.”
Then Daniel answered the king, “Keep your gifts for yourself, and give the honors of your house to others. Nevertheless, I will read the writing for the king and tell him its interpretation.”
As for you, O king, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar kingship, greatness, honor, and glory.

“Because of the greatness he gave him, all peoples, nations, and languages trembled and were afraid before him. He killed whomever he wished and kept alive whomever he wished; he raised up whomever he wished and humbled whomever he wished.”
“But when his heart became proud and his spirit grew obstinate in arrogance, he was brought down from his royal throne, and his honor was taken from him.”

“He was driven away from human beings, and his mind became like that of the wild animals. He lived with the wild donkeys, and they fed him grass like an ox. His body was drenched with the dew of heaven until his hair grew like an eagle’s feathers and his nails like a bird’s claws, until he knew that God Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity, gives it to whomever he wishes, and sets the lowliest of people over it.”
But you, his son Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, even though you knew all this.

“You raised yourself up against the Lord of heaven. They brought the vessels of his house before you, and you, your nobles, your wives, and your concubines drank wine from them. You praised the gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which cannot see or hear or know. But the God who holds your breath in his hands, and to whom all your ways belong, you did not praise or honor.”
Then the hand was sent from his presence,
and it inscribed this writing. This is the writing that was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
This is the interpretation of the matter: Mene—God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end.
Tekel—you have been weighed in the scales and found lacking.
PERES: Your kingdom is divided and given to Media and Persia.”
Then King Belshazzar gave the command, and they clothed Daniel in purple, put a gold chain around his neck, and proclaimed that he was to rule as third in the kingdom.
That very night Belshazzar, the Chaldean king, was killed.
Darius the Mede received the kingdom when he was about sixty-two years old.
Darius decided to appoint 120 military commanders throughout his kingdom.
Over them were three administrators, one of whom was Daniel, to whom these military commanders were to give an account, so that the king would suffer no harm.
Then Daniel distinguished himself above them all because an exceptional spirit was in him, and the king planned to appoint him over his entire kingdom.

Then the administrators and military commanders tried to find grounds for an accusation against Daniel concerning the affairs of the kingdom. But they could find no fault or grounds for accusation against him, because he was faithful to his God, and they found no wrongdoing or fault in him.
Those men said, “We will find no grounds for an accusation against this Daniel unless we find something against him concerning the law of his God.”
Then the administrators and military commanders approached the king and said to him, “O King Darius, live forever!”

All the rulers of the kingdom, the nobles, the military commanders, and the governors have agreed to establish a royal decree and impose a prohibition: anyone who makes a request of any god or human being for thirty days, except of you, O king, is to be thrown into the lions’ den.
Now, O king, issue this command and put it in writing, so that it cannot be changed, according to the law of Media and Persia, and cannot be altered.
Then King Darius signed the document and issued the command.

When Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went into his house. The windows of his upstairs room were open toward Jerusalem. Three times a day he knelt on his knees, prayed, and gave thanks before his God, just as he had done before.
Then those men kept watch and found Daniel making petitions and pleading before his God.

Then they approached and said before the king, “O king, live forever! Did you not issue and sign a decree, O king, that anyone who makes a request of any god or human being for thirty days, except of you, O king, is to be thrown into the lions’ den?” The king answered, “The matter is certain, according to the law of Media and Persia, which cannot be revoked.”
Then they answered and said before the king, “Daniel, one of the captives from Judah, has paid no attention to you or to the decree you issued, and he makes his petition three times.”
When the king heard this, he was deeply distressed. He set his mind on rescuing Daniel, and until sunset he struggled to rescue him.
Then those men pressed the king and said to him, “Know, O king, that Media and Persia have a law: no decree or statute established by the king may be changed.”
Then the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the lions’ den. The king said to Daniel, “May your God, whom you serve continually, rescue you.”
A stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den. The king sealed it with his signet ring and with the signet rings of his nobles, so that nothing concerning Daniel could be changed.
Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting. No food was brought before him, and sleep fled from him.
Then, in the morning, the king rose in haste and went quickly to the lions’ den.

When he approached the den, he called to Daniel in a loud voice. The king said to Daniel, “Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to rescue you from the lions?”
Then Daniel spoke to the king and said, “O king, live forever!
“My God sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not harmed me, because I was found innocent before him. Nor have I done any wrong against you, O king.”
Then the king [?] was very pleased and ordered Daniel to be brought up from the den. They brought Daniel up from the den, and no injury was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

The king said, “Bring those men who accused Daniel, and throw them into the lions’ den, along with their wives and children.” They threw them into the den, and before they reached the bottom of the den, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
Then King Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations, and language groups living throughout the earth: “May your peace increase!

“I have issued a law that throughout the dominion of my kingdom people must tremble and fear before the God of Daniel. For he is the living God, enduring forever. His kingdom will not be destroyed, and his dominion lasts to the end.
“He redeems, rescues, and delivers, and performs signs and wonders in heaven and on earth. He rescued Daniel from the lions.”
Daniel rose to greatness during the reign of Darius and during the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel had a dream and visions in his mind while on his bed. Then he wrote down the dream and related its main points.
Daniel spoke and said, “I was watching in the vision of the night, and there were the four winds of heaven stirring up the great sea.
Four great beasts came up from the sea, each different from the others.

“The first was like a lion and had eagle’s wings. I watched until its wings were plucked out, and it was lifted up from the ground and stood on its feet like a human being. A human heart was given to it.
“The second beast resembled a wolf. It stood up on one side, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. They said to it, ‘Get up! Eat much flesh!’
“After this I watched another beast, like a leopard, with four bird’s wings on its back. That beast had four heads, and dominion was given to it.

“After this I watched in the vision of the night: a fourth beast, terrifying, strong, and exceedingly powerful. It had large iron teeth. It devoured and crushed, and whatever remained it trampled with its feet. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.
“I was considering its horns, and a little horn came up among them. Three of the earlier horns were uprooted before it. That horn had eyes like human eyes and a mouth speaking boastful things.

I watched as thrones were set in place and the Ancient of Days sat down. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head was like pure wool. His throne was a flame of fire, and its wheels were burning fire.
A river of fire flowed out from before him. A thousand thousands served him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The court sat down, and the books were opened.
I watched as that beast was killed, its body was destroyed, and it was handed over to be burned with fire.
The rest of the beasts were stripped of their authority, but an extension of life was given to them for a season and a time.
I watched as someone like a human being came on the clouds of heaven. He reached the Ancient of Days, and they brought him before him.

He gave him authority, kingship, and honor, so that all peoples, nations, and languages would serve him. His authority is everlasting authority that will not pass away, and his kingdom will not be destroyed.
My spirit was distressed—I, Daniel, was in my bed—and the visions in my head troubled me.
I approached one of the attendants and asked him for the truth about all these things. He told me the truth and made known to me the interpretation of my words.
He said to me, “These four great beasts that you saw are four kings who will arise from the earth.
But the holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever, for ever and ever.”

Then I wanted to inquire about the fourth beast, which was different from all the others and exceedingly terrifying. Its teeth were iron and its claws bronze. It devoured and crushed, and whatever remained it trampled with its feet.

And I wanted to inquire about the ten horns on its head and the other horn that came up among them, before which three fell. That horn had eyes and a mouth speaking boastfully, and its appearance was greater than that of its companions.
I watched as that horn made war against the holy ones and overpowered them,
Until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment to the holy ones of the Most High, and the time arrived when the holy ones inherited the kingdom.
He said this to me: “The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom on earth. It will surpass the other kingdoms and devour the whole earth, trampling it and crushing it.
As for the ten horns, ten kings will arise from the kingdom, and another will arise after them. He will surpass the earlier ones and bring down three kings.
He will speak words against the Most High and oppress the holy ones of the Most High. He will intend to change times and laws, and they will be handed over to him for a time, times, and half a time.
The Judge sat down, and they took his authority away from him, to destroy and completely put an end to it.
For the kingship, authority, greatness, and kingdom under heaven were given to the holy people of the Most High. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all authorities will serve and obey him.”
Here the account ends. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts troubled me greatly, and my appearance changed, but I kept the matter in my heart.
In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the first vision that had appeared to me.
I saw in my dream that I was in the citadel of Susa, in the province of Elam. I saw in my dream that I was standing at the gateway of Ulai.
I looked up and saw a ram standing in front of the gateway. It had horns, and its horns were tall. One was taller than the other, and the taller one grew up last.
I saw the ram charging westward, northward, and southward. No beasts could stand before it, and none could escape its power. It did as it pleased and became great.
While I was considering this, a male goat came from the west across the whole earth without touching the ground. The goat had a conspicuous horn between its eyes.
It came up to the horned ram that I had seen standing in front of the gateway and rushed at it furiously.

It reached the ram and raged against it. It struck the ram and broke both its horns. The ram had no strength to stand against it. It threw the ram to the ground and trampled it, and there was no one to rescue the ram from the male goat's power.
The male goat became very great, but when it grew strong, its great horn was broken. Four conspicuous horns came up from beneath it toward the four winds of heaven.
From one of them came a little horn, which grew exceedingly great toward the south and toward the east.
It grew as far as the armies of heaven, cast some of the armies and some of the stars down to the earth, and trampled them.
It reached as far as the commanders of the armies, took the continual offering away from him, and demolished the established place of his sanctuary.
An army was given authority over the regular offering because of sins. The sanctuary was thrown to the ground, and it advanced and prospered.

I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to a certain one who was speaking, “How long will the vision concerning the regular offering, iniquity, and destruction be allowed to continue, and the sanctuary and the army be trampled?”
He said to him, “Until two thousand three hundred evenings and mornings; then righteousness will prevail.”
When I, Daniel, saw the vision, I sought to understand it. And there before me stood someone with the appearance of a man.
I heard a human voice from between the banks of the Ulai, calling out and saying, “Gabriel, make this man understand this vision.”
He came to where I was standing. When he came, I was afraid and fell facedown. He said to me, “Understand, human being, that this vision concerns the time of the end.”
While he was speaking with me, I fell into a stupor with my face to the ground. He touched me and made me stand upright.
He said to me, “Look, I am showing you what will happen at the end of the wrath, at the time of the end.
The ram you saw, which had horns, is the king of Media and Persia.
The male goat is the king of the Greeks, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.
As for its being broken and four arising in its place, four kings will arise from the nation, but not by their own strength.
At the end of their reign, when sins have reached their full measure, a fierce-faced king who understands riddles will arise.
His power will be strong, but not through his own strength. He will cause extraordinary destruction, succeed, and advance. He will destroy the mighty and the people of the holy ones.

Through his rule, deceit will succeed in his hands. His heart will become proud, and he will destroy many while they are at peace. He will rise against the ruler of rulers, but he will be broken by the grasp of a hand.
The vision of the morning and evening that was told is true. But you, Daniel, conceal this vision, because it concerns many days to come.
I, Daniel, trembled and was troubled for days. Then I rose and attended to the king’s business. I was astonished at the vision, but no one understood it.
In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, of Median descent, who became king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,

In the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, considered the book concerning the number of years. I saw that the word of the Lord, spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, concerned the completion of seventy years of Jerusalem’s desolation.
I lifted my face before the LORD God to seek him with prayer and supplication, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
I prayed before the Lord my God, confessed, and said, “Please, Lord, great and awe-inspiring God, who keeps the covenant and shows kindness to those who love him and keep his commandments!
We have sinned, done wrong, acted wickedly, rebelled, and turned aside from your commandments and your judgments.
We did not listen to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name concerning our kings, our leaders, our ancestors, and all the people of the land.

Righteousness belongs to you, Lord, but shame belongs to us, as it does today—to the people of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all Israel, both near and far, in all the lands where you scattered them because of the wrong they committed against you.
Lord, shame belongs to us, to our kings, our leaders, and our ancestors, because we have sinned against you.
Mercy and forgiveness of sins belong to the Lord God, though we have rebelled against him.
We did not obey the voice of the Lord our God by following his law, which he set before us through his servants the prophets.

All Israel transgressed your law and turned aside, refusing to obey your voice. You brought upon them the curses and oaths written in the law of Moses, the servant of God, because we sinned before him.
He fulfilled the words he spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, bringing upon us a great calamity. Nothing like what happened in Jerusalem has happened anywhere under heaven.
As it is written in the law of Moses, all this calamity came upon us. Yet we did not pray before the Lord our God that we might turn from our wrongdoing and understand your faithfulness.
The Lord stirred up calamity and brought it upon us, because the Lord our God is righteous in everything he has done, but we did not obey his voice.
Now, Lord our God, you brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made a name for yourself that endures to this day. We have sinned and acted wickedly.

Lord, in keeping with all the righteousness you have shown us, let your anger and fury turn away from your city Jerusalem and from your holy mountain. Because of our sins and our ancestors’ wrongdoing, your people have been scattered everywhere, and Jerusalem has become an object of scorn to all the nations.
Now, God, listen to the prayer of your servant and to our plea, and let your face shine upon your ruined sanctuary, for the sake of your name, Lord.

Incline your ear, my God, and listen. Open your eyes and see our ruins and desolate places, and the city that bears your name. For we do not rely on our righteousness when we pray before you, but on your abundant mercy.
Lord, listen! Lord, have mercy! Lord, pay attention and act! Do not delay, for the sake of your name, my God, because your city and your people bear your name.”
While I was praying and confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel, and presenting my plea before the Lord God concerning the holy mountain of my God,
while I was still speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had previously seen in the vision, came flying swiftly, soaring down from heaven, and approached me at the time of the evening offering.
He came and spoke with me, saying, “Daniel, I have now come out to teach you to understand.
“At the beginning of your prayer, a word went out, and I have come to make it known to you, because you are dearly loved. Consider the word and understand the vision.

Seventy weeks will be allotted to your people and your holy city, to bring transgressions to an end, to finish sins, to forgive wrongdoing, to bring everlasting righteousness, to fulfill the vision and the prophets, and to anoint the most holy.

Know and understand: from the issuing of the word to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the coming of the Anointed One, the king, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. He will return and rebuild Jerusalem, its streets and its squares, until the end of the time.

After the sixty-two weeks, the Anointed One will be killed and have nothing. The holy city will be destroyed along with the king who is coming. Its end will be in a flood, and until the end of the war there will be decreed devastation.

He will strengthen a covenant for many for one week and half a week, and he will abolish sacrifice and offerings. On the wings of defilement there will be devastation, until the full completion of what has been decreed rests upon the destroyer.”

In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a message was revealed to Daniel, who was called Belteshazzar. The message was true and concerned a great force. He understood the message and gained understanding of it through the vision.
In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three full weeks.
I ate no choice bread; no meat or wine entered my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with oil until the three weeks were over.
On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was beside the great river, the Euphrates.
I raised my eyes and looked, and there was a man dressed in splendid clothing, with his waist girded in glorious splendor.

His appearance was extraordinary and had no likeness. His face was like lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and shoulders like gleaming bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of many armies.
I, Daniel, alone saw this vision. The men who were with me did not see it, but great terror fell upon them, and they fled in fear.
I was left alone and saw this great vision. No strength remained in me; my insides began to waste away, and I had no strength.
When I heard the sound of his words, I fell face down on the ground.
Then a hand touched me and raised me onto my knees and the palms of my hands.
He said to me, “Rise, Daniel, dearly loved man. Understand the words I am speaking to you, and stand upright, for I have now been sent to you.” As he spoke these words to me, I stood trembling.
He said to me, “Do not be afraid, Daniel, for from the first day you set your heart on understanding and on standing before your God, your words were heard, and I have come because of your words.
The ruler of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the foremost princes, came to help me, and I remained there opposing the ruler of Persia.
I have come to show you what will happen to your people in the last days, for the vision still concerns the end of days.”
As he spoke these words to me, I lowered my face to the ground and remained silent.

Then someone resembling a human being touched my lips. I opened my mouth and spoke, saying to the one standing before me, “My lord, because of the vision my insides have turned against me, and I have been unable to stand.
How can the servant of this lord of mine speak with this lord of mine? There is no strength in me, and no breath remains in me.”
Again, the one with a human appearance touched me and strengthened me.
He said to me, “Do not be afraid, dearly loved man. Peace be with you! Be strong and courageous.” As he spoke to me, I was strengthened, and I said, “Let my lord speak, for I have been strengthened.”
He said to me, “Do you know why I have come to you? Now I will return to fight against the ruler of Persia. When I go out, the ruler of the Greeks will come.
But I will show you what is recorded in the book of truth. No one helps me in all these things except Michael, your ruler.
And as for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, he stood up to strengthen and support me.

Now I will tell you the truth. Three more kings will arise in Persia, and a fourth will acquire far greater wealth than all of them. When he has become strong in his land, he will stir up all the kingdoms of the Greeks.
A mighty king will arise and rule with great authority, doing as he pleases.

When he has arisen, his kingdom will be broken and scattered to the four winds of heaven. It will not belong to his descendants or have the authority with which he ruled. Instead, his kingdom will be uprooted, and there will be no other apart from these.
The king of the south and his princes will grow strong, and one will become stronger than he and rule with great authority.

After some years they will reach an agreement. The daughter of the king of the south will go to the king of the north to make peace between them. But she will have no strength because of the fear that will seize her. She will be handed over, along with those who brought her, her young women, and those who supported her at that time.
Someone from the root of his offspring will arise in his place. He will come with an army and advance in strength against the king of the north. He will sweep through them and grow strong.
He will also take their gods, their precious vessels of silver and gold, and captives down to Egypt. He himself will stand against the king of the north for a time or two.
He will enter the stronghold of the king of the south and return to his own land.
His sons will wage war and gather large armies. They will advance against him, sweep through like a flood, and pass on. They will return and wage war as far as the fortress.
The king of the south will become enraged and go out to meet the king of the north. He will muster a great army, and that army will be delivered into his hand.
He will destroy the army, and his heart will become proud. He will bring down many, but he will not grow strong.
The king of the north will return and muster an army larger than the first. After a time or two, he will advance with a large army and powerful cavalry.
At that time many will rise against the king of the north. Wicked men among your people will rise up to fulfill the vision, but they will be overthrown.

The king of the north will come, set ambushes, and capture strong fortresses. The forces of the south will not stand, because they have no strength to resist. The chosen men of the people will take their stand, but they will not succeed, because they have no strength to resist.
The one who comes against him will do as he pleases, and no one will stand before him. He will take his stand in the land of Israel, and it will be delivered into his hands.

He will set his face to enter with the strength of all the kingdoms, and all his people will pass through. A daughter will be given to him to destroy him, but she will not stand firm or belong to him.
He will turn his face toward the islands of the sea and conquer many. The ruler who was insulting him will come to an end, and he will turn his insult back on him.
He will turn his face toward the stronghold of the land, but he will be overthrown and fall, and he will not be found.
In his place will arise someone who takes away dominion and the splendor of kings. Within a few days he will be broken, not through anger or [?].
A weak man will arise in his place, and royal splendor will not be bestowed on him. He will come quietly and seize the kingdom through deceit.
The strength of the fortified cities will be plundered, and they will be broken before him, as will the leaders of the covenant.
Those who ally themselves with him will plot against him. He will rise and grow strong with a small people.

In the richest parts of the cities he will do what neither his fathers nor his fathers’ fathers did. He will carry off plunder, captives, and their possessions. He will devise plans against their fortresses, but only until a certain time.

His strength and courage will be stirred up against the king of the south with a great and powerful army. The king of the south will be roused to battle with a great army and become exceedingly strong, but he will not stand, because plans will be devised against him.
Those who eat his royal food will break him. His army will be scattered, and many will fall slain.
Both these kings will have their hearts set on evil. They will speak deceitfully at one table, but they will not succeed, because the end will arrive at its appointed time.
He will return to his land with a large army. His heart will be set against the holy covenant, and he will act.
As at the beginning, so also at the end.
The armies of Kittim will come against him and defeat him. He will return and rage against the holy covenant, and he will give his attention to those who have abandoned the holy covenant.
Their forces will arise from among them. They will defile the fortified sanctuary, remove the offerings, and set up a defilement that brings destruction.
He will condemn those who transgress the covenant, but the people who know the faith will grow strong.
The righteous among the people will teach many, but they will fall by the sword and by fire, through captivity and plunder, for a thousand days.
When they are overthrown, they will receive a little help, and many will join them with divided loyalty.
Some of the wise will fall, so that they may be tested and gain discernment until the time of the end, because there is still a delay until the appointed time.
The king will do as he pleases and exalt himself above every god. He will speak boastfully against the God of gods and prosper until the wrath is completed, because what was decreed has been done.
He will pay no attention to the God of his fathers. He will have no regard for the desire of women or for any god, but will exalt himself above everything.
He will honor a mighty god in his place. He will honor a god whom his fathers did not know with gold, silver, precious stones, and desirable things.
He will pass into the strong fortresses, against foreign gods whom he will see. He will rule over many and divide the land for a price.
At the time of the end, the king of the south will fight with him. The king of the north will rush against him with chariots, horsemen, and many ships, and he will enter the land.
He will reach the land of Israel, and many will be killed. But these will escape from his hands: Edom, Moab, and the remainder of the Ammonites.
He will stretch out his hand against the countries, and the land of Egypt will not escape his hands.
He will control the treasury of gold and silver and all the desirable things of Egypt. The Libyans and Cushites will come to his aid.
Reports from the east and the north will alarm him, and he will go out in great fury to devastate and destroy many.
He will pitch his tent in an open place between the sea and the mountain and guard his sanctuary. The time of his end will arrive, and he will have no helper.

At that time Michael, the great angel appointed over your people, will arise. There will be a time of distress unlike anything that has happened since ancient times. At that time, everyone among your people who is found written in the book will be delivered.
Many of those who sleep in the dust will awake: some to everlasting life, and others to destruction and the reproach of their companions forever.
Those who do good and those who have understanding will shine like the brightness of the sky. Those who make many righteous will shine and endure like the stars forever and ever.
But you, Daniel, seal these words and remain silent. Seal this book until the time of the end. Many will search, and knowledge will increase.
I, Daniel, looked, and there were two others standing there, one on this bank of the river and one on the other.
They said to the man dressed in splendid clothes who stood above the waters of the river, “How long until this end?”

And I heard the man who was dressed in splendid clothes and stood above the waters of the river. He raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and swore by the one who lives forever that it would be for a time, times, and half a time, and that when the hands of all the holy people are set free, all these things would be completed.
I, Daniel, heard but did not understand. I said, “My lord, what comes after these things?”
He said to me, “Go, Daniel, for the words are hidden and sealed until the time of the end.
Many will be chosen, made white, and tested. Sinners will sin, and none of the sinners will understand, but those who do good will understand.
From the time the offering is removed and the abomination is set up to bring destruction, there will be 1,290 days.
Blessed is the one who waits and reaches 1,335 days.
But you, Daniel, go to the end. Rest, and you will arise at your appointed time, at the end of the days.”
